newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN DIRECTORS URGE FASTER ECONOMIC REFORM.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN DIRECTORS URGE FASTER ECONOMIC REFORM.

text.p: The president of the Australian Institute of Company Directors, John Ralph said on Thursday Australia was showing signs of economic 'reform fatigue' as a consequence of the reform process being too slow and unbalanced.
Ralph, who is also chairman of Foster's Brewing Group Ltd and deputy chairman of Telstra Corp, told a luncheon that the reform process had lost momentum and was in danger of falling over.
"If we are to have a more competitive economy able to meet the reasonable aspirations of Australians, it is not less reform but faster more balanced reform that is required," he said.
Ralph said Australia did not have mutually-reinforcing reforms that characterise countries which have been the most successful in tackling the problem of unemployment.

Tax was one area which was ripe for reform, Ralph said, especially after the decision earlier this week of the High Court to strike down the rights of states to impose fees and charges on retailers of tobacco, alcohol and petrol.

"This latest decision further supports the need for a fundamental review and restructuring of the tax system and for a review of the constitutional arrangements between the Commonwealth and the States," he said.
"Fiddling at the edges will not be good enough," Ralph said.

He said the criteria for a desirable tax system should not be about how government could more easily collect revenues but how the system should be structured to to deliver maximum economic performance and to create the greatest number of wealth-creating jobs in the community.
Ralph said he was a long-time advocate of a broad-based consumption tax but said tax reform needed to go beyond just considering whether to introduce this tax.
